title: Lake Lisan
summary: Lake Lisan was the late Pleistocene precursor of the Dead Sea. Bartov and colleagues put it at about 70,000 to 15,000 years ago; it rose sharply from about 27,000 years ago to a peak near 164 m below sea level between 26,000 and 23,000 years ago, then fell to about 300 m below sea level as it shrank towards the Dead Sea.

uncertainty.note: Years used as stated with no offset. Bartov et al. (2002) cover 55,000 to 15,000 cal yr BP and give the highstand as 26,000 to 23,000; GFZ places highstand sediments between about 24,000 and 14,000 years ago.

as_recorded.value: highstand between ca 24.000 and 14.000 years ago

when.display: c. 70,000 to 15,000 years ago (highstand c. 26,000 to 23,000)

where.modern_name: Dead Sea basin (proxy pin at the modern Dead Sea), Israel, Jordan and the West Bank
where.historical_name: Lake Lisan, Jordan Rift Valley, before any states

importance.justification: Records the last-glacial water balance of the Levant and fed the salt and sediment record of the Dead Sea.

sources.title: Lake Levels and Sequence Stratigraphy of Lake Lisan, the Late Pleistocene Precursor of the Dead Sea
sources.author: Yuval Bartov, Mordechai Stein, Yehouda Enzel, Amotz Agnon, Ze'ev Reches

sources.title: News from the climate history of the Dead Sea
sources.publisher: GFZ German Research Centre for Geosciences

reviewer_note: Least sure of the period: the 70,000 start is the summary on the Cambridge page, while the study itself covers 55,000 to 15,000 cal yr BP, and GFZ gives a 24,000 to 14,000 highstand. The pin is a proxy at the modern Dead Sea; the lake was far larger. Years are as stated, no offset.
